In 1994, Schmidt and [Nicholas B. Suntzeff](/wiki/Nicholas_B._Suntzeff "Nicholas B. Suntzeff") formed the [High-Z Supernova Search Team](/wiki/High-Z_Supernova_Search_Team "High-Z Supernova Search Team") to measure the expected deceleration of the universe and the [deceleration parameter](/wiki/Deceleration_parameter "Deceleration parameter") (q0) using distances to [Type Ia supernovae](/wiki/Type_Ia_supernovae "Type Ia supernovae"). In 1995, the HZT at a meeting at the [Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian](/wiki/Harvard-Smithsonian_Center_for_Astrophysics "Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics") elected Schmidt as the overall leader of the HZT. Schmidt led the team from Australia and in 1998 in the HZT paper with first author [Adam Riess](/wiki/Adam_Riess "Adam Riess") the first evidence was presented that the universe's expansion rate is not decelerating; it is accelerating.[[17]](#cite_note-17) The team's observations were contrary to the then-current models, which predicted that the expansion of the universe should be slowing down, and when the preliminary results emerged Schmidt assumed it was an error and he spent the next six weeks trying to find the mistake.[[18]](#cite_note-Our_Strange_Universe-18) But there was no mistake: contrary to expectations, by monitoring the brightness and measuring the [redshift](/wiki/Redshift "Redshift") of the [supernovae](/wiki/Supernovae "Supernovae"), they discovered that these billion-year old exploding stars and their galaxies were accelerating away from our reference frame.[[19]](#cite_note-bbc_nobel-19) This result was also found nearly simultaneously by the [Supernova Cosmology Project](/wiki/Supernova_Cosmology_Project "Supernova Cosmology Pro

While not precisely autobiographical, much of Saint-Exupéry's work is inspired by his experiences as a pilot. One notable example is his novella, *[The Little Prince](/wiki/The_Little_Prince "The Little Prince"),* a poetic tale self-illustrated in watercolours in which a pilot stranded in the desert meets a young prince fallen to Earth from a tiny [asteroid](/wiki/Asteroid "Asteroid"). "His most popular work, *The Little Prince* was partially based upon a crash he and his navigator survived in the Libyan desert. They were stranded and dehydrated for four days, nearing death when they miraculously stumbled upon a Bedouin who gave them water."[[85]](#cite_note-100) Saint-Exupéry wrote in *Wind, Sand and Stars* that the Bedouin saved their lives and gave them "charity and magnanimity [by] bearing the gift of water." *The Little Prince* is a philosophical story, including societal criticism, remarking on the strangeness of the adult world. One biographer wrote of his most famous work: "Rarely have an author and a character been so intimately bound together as Antoine de Saint-Exupéry and his Little Prince," and remarking of their dual fates, "...the two remain tangled together, twin innocents who fell from the sky."[[26]](#cite_note-NYT2000-28)

In France, the Sémillon grape is grown mostly in Bordeaux where it is blended with [Sauvignon blanc](/wiki/Sauvignon_blanc "Sauvignon blanc") and [Muscadelle](/wiki/Muscadelle "Muscadelle").[[6]](#cite_note-6) When dry, it is referred to as *Bordeaux blanc* and is permitted to be made in the appellations of [Pessac-Léognan](/wiki/Pessac-L%C3%A9ognan "Pessac-Léognan"), [Graves](/wiki/Graves_(wine_region) "Graves (wine region)"), [Entre-Deux-Mers](/wiki/Entre-Deux-Mers "Entre-Deux-Mers") and other less-renowned regions. In this form, Sémillon is generally a minor constituent in the blend. However, when used to make the sweet white wines of Bordeaux (such as those from Sauternes, Barsac and Cérons) it is often the dominant variety.[[3]](#cite_note-oxf-sem-3) In such wines the vine is exposed to the "[noble rot](/wiki/Noble_rot "Noble rot")" of *[Botrytis cinerea](/wiki/Botrytis_cinerea "Botrytis cinerea")* which consumes the water content of the fruit, concentrating the sugar present in its pulp. When attacked by Botrytis cinerea, the grapes shrivel and the acid and sugar levels are intensified.[[7]](#cite_note-epi-7)

Due to the declining popularity of the grape variety, fewer clones are cultivated in nurseries causing producers to project a future shortage of quality wine. In 2008, 17 Bordeaux wine producers, including [Château d'Yquem](/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_d%27Yquem "Château d'Yquem"), [Château Olivier](/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_Olivier "Château Olivier"), [Château Suduiraut](/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_Suduiraut "Château Suduiraut") and [Château La Tour Blanche](/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_La_Tour_Blanche "Château La Tour Blanche"), formed an association to grow their own clones.[[8]](#cite_note-deca08-8)

After a period of volatility, the global PC market began to stabilize in 2023. According to IDC, worldwide PC shipments during the fourth quarter of 2024 grew 1.8% year-over-year, reaching 68.9 million units.[[97]](#cite_note-97) Canalys reported a 3.2% annual growth in the first quarter of 2024, totaling 57.2 million units, with notebook shipments increasing by 4.2%.[[98]](#cite_note-98)

In the first quarter of 2025, global PC shipments experienced a significant uptick, growing 9.4% year-over-year to 62.7 million units. This surge was partly attributed to manufacturers accelerating shipments to the U.S. ahead of newly implemented tariffs under President Donald Trump's trade policies. Lenovo maintained its lead in the global PC market, shipping 15.2 million units with an 11% growth, followed by HP with 12.8 million units (6% growth), Dell with 9.5 million units (3% growth), and Apple with 6.5 million units, marking a 22% increase.[[99]](#cite_note-99) The integration of [artificial intelligence](/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") (AI) capabilities into PCs emerged as a significant trend during this period.

[Box Office Mojo](/wiki/Box_Office_Mojo "Box Office Mojo") estimates that after adjusting for the rise in average ticket prices, *Avatar* would be the 14th-highest-grossing film of all time in the United States and Canada.[[212]](#cite_note-235) On a worldwide basis, when *Avatar*'s gross stood at $2 billion after 35 days in theaters, *[The Daily Telegraph](/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")* estimated its [inflation](/wiki/Inflation "Inflation")-adjusted gross was surpassed only by *[Gone with the Wind](/wiki/Gone_with_the_Wind_(film) "Gone with the Wind (film)")* ($3.0 billion), *[Titanic](/wiki/Titanic_(1997_film) "Titanic (1997 film)")* ($2.9 billion), and *[Star Wars](/wiki/Star_Wars_(film) "Star Wars (film)")* ($2.2 billion).[[213]](#cite_note-236)[[6]](#cite_note-BOM-8) [Reuters](/wiki/Reuters "Reuters") and the 2015 edition of [Guinness World Records](/wiki/Guinness_World_Records "Guinness World Records") placed *Avatar* ahead of *Titanic* after adjusting for inflation.[[x]](#cite_note-240)
